summary_1line: Pandavas move from Dwaitavana after Yudhishthira dreams of pleading deer, endure exile hardship, and receive Vyasa’s counsel on patience and ascetic endurance.

image_candidates.scene_text: In a dream, trembling deer with folded forelegs stand before Yudhishthira in the dark forest, pleading for mercy and a chance to survive.
The Pandavas and Draupadi depart Dwaitavana with Brahmanas and attendants, walking along forest roads toward the sacred woods of Kamyaka.
The sage Vyasa, eyes moist with compassion, looks upon the thin and weary Pandavas living on fruits and roots in their forest hermitage.
